name: Postcardiotomy Right Ventricular Failure
aliases: Right Ventricular Failure after Cardiac Surgery

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Postcardiotomy Right Ventricular Failure Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Persistent hemodynamic instability despite adequate left ventricular function post-cardiac surgery
Echocardiographic evidence of right ventricular dilation and reduced right ventricular systolic function
Elevated central venous pressure (>15 mmHg) with low cardiac output
Exclusion of other causes of hemodynamic compromise such as tamponade or left ventricular failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hemodynamic instability with echocardiographic evidence of RV dysfunction and elevated central venous pressure after cardiac surgery
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging and hemodynamic monitoring; exclusion of other postoperative complications is essential.

searchTerms: elevated pressure in large veins near heart

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hemodynamic instability refractory to volume resuscitation
searchTerms: unstable blood flow not fixed by fluids
shock not improved with volume replacement

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to low cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output
weakness from heart not pumping well

occasional.symptomName: Elevated liver enzymes secondary to congestion
searchTerms: liver damage due to blood backup
elevated liver tests from fluid overload
blood clot in right heart chamber

rare.symptomName: Renal dysfunction secondary to low perfusion
searchTerms: kidney problems from low blood flow
renal dysfunction due to poor perfusion

laboratory: Elevated liver transaminases due to hepatic congestion
Possible elevated serum lactate due to low cardiac output
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular dilation and reduced systolic function
Right heart catheterization demonstrating elevated right atrial and pulmonary artery pressures
Chest X-ray may show cardiomegaly and pleural effusions
other: Hemodynamic monitoring indicating low cardiac output with preserved left ventricular function
Exclusion of pericardial tamponade or left ventricular failure

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction
Pulmonary edema more prominent than systemic venous congestion
Pericardial effusion with diastolic collapse of right atrium or ventricle
Acute onset dyspnea and chest pain
Elevated D-dimer and right ventricular strain pattern

redFlags: Signs of systemic venous congestion with worsening organ dysfunction
Development of ventricular arrhythmias or cardiac arrest
references: Katz AM. Physiology of the heart. 5th ed. Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2010.
